name: 2026-09-16-creator-persistent-plugin-management
title: Creator mode installs persistent plugin bundles

attrs.decision:
Creator mode enables the existing `plugin_manager` tool. Agents author packages and Loader YAML patches as workspace files, then install them through `install_bundle`. An MCP connection is a configuration-only bundle inserting the installed `dsh-mcp-client`; a UI bundle includes a Host entry and a Client artifact. name: 2026-09-16-experimental-voice-input
title: Experimental voice input with explicit recognition providers

attrs.decision:

The browser UI dynamically mounts its generated Remote contribution. Stable API Remotes do not acquire an experimental dependency.

name: 2026-09-16-host-schedule-storage

name: 2026-09-16-user-terminal-permissions

name: 2026-09-17-account-provider-signout
title: Account provider and active request cancellation

name: 2026-09-17-developer-session-changes

The header reference is absent when the message contains no additions. Same-name replacement, restart, fork, and surface replacement retain historical definition identity without consulting the current registry or latest request header. name: 2026-09-17-process-local-blank-sessions
title: Writer acquisition for blank Session reuse

attrs.decision:
The Session catalog includes persisted blanks. Startup restoration selects the saved blank; ordinary Workspace navigation selects the first eligible unarchived member in catalog order. Other errors propagate. A Workspace connect in one Client joins the latest in-flight connect to that Workspace only when both request the same preset. Later navigation cancels a pending startup selection.

The Agent retains the acquired handle throughout its lifetime. Checking ownership and releasing a probe lock would leave a race before resume. No PID or process identity enters persisted data or the Remote schema.

name: 2026-09-20-device-local-shortcut-preferences

name: 2026-09-21-desktop-page-close-shortcuts

name: 2026-10-09-operator-scoped-connect-handshake

name: 2026-10-09-ptc-owned-policy-cleanup
title: PTC owns policy-change cleanup waits

attrs.decision:
Permission setters commit synchronously. Success means the selected policy is recorded; it does not guarantee that operations admitted under the old policy have completely stopped. This replaces the completion requirement and cleanup ownership in the [retained-process sandbox decision](2026-10-08-persistent-ptc-sandbox.md), whose confinement and one-time escalation rules still apply.

PTC observes committed Session mode changes. The tool bridge immediately cancels affected complete calls, including pending approvals and nested tools. A later PTC call waits for canceled predecessors to settle before resolving the latest standing policy. The Node provider immediately invalidates affected processes, including idle environments, starts cleanup, and retains the cleanup Promise internally. A later program waits for that cleanup; failed cleanup remains retryable and prevents process reuse. Unchanged modes preserve environments. Tool-registry and provider unload remove their observers and await owned work.
attrs.problem: Stopping a retained Node process and its nested tools can take longer than recording a new file policy. Making permission setters await that cleanup spreads PTC lifecycle requirements into unrelated callers, including Webhook Session creation, and adds cancellation windows to those callers.

name: 2026-10-19-cua-profile-consent-storage
title: Durable Computer Use consent within one profile

attrs.decision:
The CUA owner uses the existing domain storage service, with one domain per canonical profile directory. It stores long-term grants and conversation decisions by native application identity. The native identity policy remains owned by [bundle-ID consent](2026-10-25-cua-bundle-id-consent.md); this note replaces only that note's storage and restart-lifetime choices.

Native dispatch and revocation use a separate lock for the selected application. Storage reads and unrelated applications remain available during a native call. Revocation cancels this process's affected work first, then commits after other processes' already-admitted operations have finished. A completed revocation therefore leaves no operation using the old authority. App-wide revocation generations and per-conversation decision revisions prevent an old handle or delayed answer from restoring revoked access.

name: 2026-10-19-file-drag-plugin-ownership

name: 2026-10-19-pi-ai-system-reminder-fallback
title: Pi-ai system reminder fallback

attrs.decision:
The pi-ai adapter uses the prepared model's existing `supportsMidConvoSystemMessages` capability mapping. name: 2026-10-19-team-task-board-inbox
title: Team task boards share ordinary subagent waits

name: 2026-10-20-new-session-blank-reuse-by-preset

name: 2026-10-21-session-history-stream-and-snapshot
title: Session snapshots, passive subscriptions, and Web aggregation

`SessionController` is the single Session Remote Service. It owns ordinary `HistoryController`, `StateController`, and `WebController` instances, not three additional Cordis Services or Remote namespaces. The implementation separates six operations: history snapshot and observation, projection snapshot and observation, and state snapshot and observation. Follow and Wait compose those capabilities for their callers; the existing `page` entry forwards to the history reader.

name: 2026-10-22-subagent-target-user-controls
title: User controls address the target subagent

Browser prompts and `interruptByUser` address only the target child Session. Prompt delivery derives the live root from the resident Activation or verified persisted creation edges. Only the cold target resumes; its creator can remain offline. name: 2026-10-23-independent-session-forks
title: Ordinary forks have no durable creator relationship

Ordinary forks preserve their complete selected prefix, `isSeeded`, `inheritedEventCount`, and inherited end-seed marker, but record no source id. name: 2026-10-29-retained-ptc-interruption
title: Retained PTC interruption

attrs.decision:
The host revokes execution authority immediately and requests cooperative stop over the existing control channel. The runtime rejects pending bindings; the original `run()` response confirms that evaluation has settled. Revocation is a one-way notification. The ordered pipe and single active evaluation determine notification ownership; RPC requests associate replies with callers. Acknowledgment permits reuse of the VM and retained objects; earlier mutations remain. Callers await acknowledgment or fallback process cleanup before starting another evaluation.

The host bounds acknowledgment with `stopGraceMs`. Missing or failed acknowledgment terminates the managed process range and awaits cleanup. Results retain the original timeout or cancellation kind and report whether variables survived. Confirmed termination allows a fresh environment on the next call; failed cleanup blocks reuse until host release succeeds. Explicit reset, disposal and policy invalidation terminate immediately. Reset uses the existing release path and exposes no additional model tool.
attrs.problem: Terminating a retained Node process on every timeout or cancellation loses unrelated application objects and imported modules. A control handler on the evaluation thread cannot stop a synchronous loop. The [in-memory execution decision](2026-09-23-best-effort-persistent-ptc.md) still owns disposable state and Session behavior; this decision replaces its timeout and cancellation cleanup policy.
